decisions.w6_gap: Build W5 bilingual and staged. Both locales' prompt text lives in W5-owned files; window phrases / a11y labels / month names live in a W5-local src/lib/memory/copy.ts staging post, the same pattern W3 used for src/app/onboarding/copy.ts. Side prompts carry their own format rules rather than forking base.ts, which is W6's file. English is unreachable at runtime until W6 flips users.locale.
decisions.week_start: Monday (ISO-8601). Plan open question 1, settled with Miftah 2026-07-27.
decisions.birthday_window: Collapses to [today, today] on the birthday itself; the gate hides it. Plan open question 2, settled with Miftah 2026-07-27.
decisions.cross_reader_recall: Left as M12 specifies: on by default, with the reader named in the block. Plan open question 5 stays open pending one real read on hardware.

findings.dilution_inverted: The chain block was expected to dilute the 40-word paragraph ceiling. Measured with fixed hands: Margaret 312 words without it, 216 with. The block makes her SHORTER -- the instruction restating the ceiling more than pays for the added context.
findings.pre_existing_regression: Margaret's spread3 runs at 312 words in the control, against the 128-169 band in CLAUDE.md. Not W5's: the system prompt with memory:null is byte-identical to what shipped before, and there is a test asserting it. Surfaced by W5's new per-paragraph word count. Fixing it means readers.ts or services.ts and its own tuning loop.
findings.chain_ratio: 2/9 (22%), inside the 15-60% band. Both via the phrase signal, none via the card signal.
findings.tuning_passes: Three. Day summary 61->53->43 words for Margaret; frequency line 29->22. Both fixed by the services.ts pattern: a ceiling stated as 'N sentences AND M words, whichever first', bound explicitly on the long-sentence reader, and restated AFTER whatever invites elaboration.
